newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Resources steer Australia stocks to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Resources steer Australia stocks to higher close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2699 +7 US 30yr cl 6.49 +0.01
10yrbond futs 93.385 -0.075 Gold NY 323.75 Lon fix 319.40
*Stocks make moderate gains pre-weekend, miners make most gains, golds shine. Volume 307.50 million, A$680.81 million, 1,105 stocks traded, 307 steady, 486 up, 312 down.
The Australian share market locked away most of its early gains by the close on Friday with a stronger resources group leading the way higher.
The All Ordinaries index climbed 14.5 points to 2,684.2, while September share price index futures contracts were seven points up at 2,699, a 14.8 point premium to the underlying index.

Miners managed more than twice the rise of the industrials with the benefits of a weaker Australian dollar and firmer base metals prices boosting the leaders, while the bounce in the bullion price pushed the gold sector to a 1.3 percent gain.
"The golds jumped and you may see the gold price go a little further tonight," said dealer Grant Williams of Reynolds and Co.
Others agreed, noting those who had backed the sector after the recent selloff had posted impressive returns.
"The brave ones who backed their judgement when gold was down in the dumps have obviously come out quite well," said Hartley Poynton broker, Dirk Van der Struyf.

In the golds, Acacia Resources added 2.9 percent to A$1.38, sector heavyweight Normandy Mining jumped 2.6 percent to A$1.57, while mooted takeover target Great Central Mines climbed 1.9 percent to A$2.69.

Key miners BHP, up 10 cents to A$18.56, Rio Tinto 24 cents higher at A$21.80, and WMC, 21 cents stronger at A$7.87, all benefited from from a weaker Australian dollar and base metals prices that firmed up offshore.

Shares in soft drink maker Coca-Cola Amatil belied the general sluggishness in industrials, rocketing A$1.53 to A$16.58 with traders saying sentiment appeared to have turned for the stock in the absence of major news.
Elsewhere, pay tv operator Australis Media ended up 1.5 cents at 21.5 cents with 6.9 million shares traded after the stock was reinstated to trading mid-morning.
The company said it was still in possible merger talks with rival operator, Foxtel, jointly owned by News Corp and Telstra Corp, the government owned telecommunications carrier.
Expectations for the next week were squarely focussed on second quarter inflation data, due Wednesday, with the hopes for interest rate cuts still alive.

"That will be the issue. The market has been reasonably directionless this week as far as economic news goes, and next week figures come out that we will be focussing closely on," said Daiwa Securities dealer, Michael Sichlau.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian bond yields finished higher, reflecting extreme weakness in the neighbouring New Zealand market and further softness in U.S. Treasuries during Tokyo trading. By 5.10 p.m. (0710 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.63 percent, compared to Thursday's 6.55 percent.

The Australian dollar reached its highest level in a week as it broke through resistance on short-covering, with comments from a former Reserve Bank of Australia governor ahead of a key data next week also helping.

By 5.10 p.m. (0710 GMT), the dollar was at US$0.7386/91, having reached a week high of US$0.7399, from an early US$0.7349/54 and Thursday's close of US$0.7365/70. ------------------------(TECHNICALS)--------------------------- Short-term range Support Restnce RSI-14 MA-10 MA-20
